mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Velar P380 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full reconditioned or rebuilt Range Rover Velar P380 engine typically costs between £4,500 and £9,500 for the unit itself, depending on the level of rebuild.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of supercharger failure in a Range Rover Velar P380?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your AJ126 engine. Listen for a distinct rattling or whining noise from the supercharger nose at idle or on deceleration. Look for unexplained oil consumption or oil leaks contaminating the accessory drive belts.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Velar P380?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, absolutely, given the high retained values of the L560 supercharged V6 Velar range. A rebuilt AJ126 engine with upgraded supercharger couplers and cooling components can extend the vehicle's life significantly. For vehicles valued over £18,000, a warranted reconditioned engine protects your investment far better than a cheap used unit.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the P380 and P400 Velar engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The P380 uses a 3.0-litre supercharged V6 (AJ126) producing 380 PS, offering classic supercharged throttle response. The P400 (introduced in 2020) uses a 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six mild-hybrid (AJ20P6) producing 400 PS, prioritising efficiency and electric torque fill.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Velar P380 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straightforward supply and fit of a reconditioned AJ126 engine typically takes 3 to 5 days at a specialist workshop. This allows time for proper bedding-in procedures, ECU calibration, fluid checks, and a thorough road test to ensure the V6 powertrain is performing flawlessly.

problems.h4: Supercharger Coupler & Bearing Wear - Why the Range Rover Velar P380 AJ126 Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: The supercharger nose coupler degrades over time, causing a distinct rattling noise at idle, while bearing wear can lead to oil contamination of the drive belts and eventual supercharger seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coupler, inspect bearings, flush oil, and verify drive belt integrity.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early and there is no secondary internal engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the supercharger has seized or the engine has suffered secondary damage.

problems.recommendation: If your Velar P380 is exhibiting early signs of supercharger rattle or minor coolant seepage, a preventative specialist service is a cost-effective solution. However, if the engine has suffered severe overheating or internal damage, a full reconditioned replacement is the most reliable long-term investment to preserve the vehicle's performance and value.

problems.h4: Cooling System & Crossover Pipe Leaks - Why the Range Rover Velar P380 Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: Plastic coolant crossover pipes located in the engine valley become brittle under extreme heat cycling, leading to sudden coolant loss and potential overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace plastic pipes with upgraded aluminium components and flush the system.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as preventative maintenance to avoid catastrophic overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if severe coolant loss has caused the engine to overheat and warp the cylinder heads.
